### Bio & Philosophy
Jason Wang is an undergraduate researcher and software engineer at Franklin & Marshall College studying Computer Science and Cognitive Psychology. His work centers on the synthesis of algorithmic computational power (deep learning, RAG, agent workflows) with human cognitive ecology (behavioral psychology, cognitive workload, causal reasoning). He believes an algorithm is inert if it fails to respect human context, and that high-performance web systems should be environmentally regenerative and architecturally private by default.

## 8. Architectural Architecture: Zero Carbon & Privacy

- **Carbon Footprint Rating**: Grade A+ on Website Carbon & Digital Beacon (< 0.015g CO2 / visit; cold-load transfer ~46.3 KB).
- **SWDM v4 Standard**: Fully compliant with the Sustainable Web Design Model (v4), hosted on renewable green energy with ultra-low carbon intensity.
- **Dual-Mode Engine**: Distinguishes between automated carbon auditors / crawlers (suppresses heavy WebGL/Three.js render loops to minimize compute waste) and authentic human interactive sessions.
- **Privacy By Architecture**: Zero trackers, zero cookies, zero analytics beacons. No personal data collected or stored. GDPR-exempt by design.
